prospect.training_background: Roughly 20 minutes of daily morning gymnastics — stretching plus some light push-ups — for the last two to two and a half years. Previously five years of intermittent gym membership with long gaps, plus swimming 40-45 minutes, all self-programmed from YouTube. Never worked with a personal trainer by choice. prospect.medical: Volunteered a diagnosis he named as 'holesteric or metabolic syndrome' and said he restricts sweets because of it. Two and a half years ago, aged 41-42, had a combined episode of kidney stones passing plus a bladder infection presenting with haematuria and pain; believed for one to two months that it was prostate cancer before it was ruled out. That scare is what triggered his nutrition changes and his adoption of 24-36 hour fasting. Reports no current aches, pains or stiffness. The rep never asked about health conditions at any point; both disclosures were volunteered.

Offered a three-payment split and volunteered that three payments stay at $6,000 total while six payments rise to $7,200, steering him to three.

offer.payment_plan_terms: Rep stated the tiering explicitly: three payments hold the total at $6,000, six payments raise the total to $7,200. He recommended three — 'on free [three] payments it would stay a total of $6,000 but if we go to six payments that would make it go up to $72[00]... I would suggest that we just do it in three times.' No dates or amounts per instalment were fixed. Payment mechanism unresolved.

evidence: No payment taken and no payment link sent; the prospect has no credit card and no mechanism was agreed.
Explicit deferral for financial calculation: 'I have to calculate anyway. I think, I think yes, but anyway, I have to check it' and 'I need one week'.
Follow-up agreed for Thursday the following week: 'let's just speak to each other again on Thursday, and then from on there... we just need to figure it out with your friends.'

Counter-evidence on intent: high engagement throughout, a clean commitment check ('No. There is no reason' not to get there), and a stated integrity frame — 'I am kind of person, when we shake hands, when we have agreement, you have to follow it'.
Counter-evidence against: month-end surplus is sometimes zero, he supports seven-plus dependants, income has a variable component, and he is relocating with children in the follow-up window.
outcome.next_step: Prospect to calculate what instalment structure he can commit to; call again Thursday the following week, then resolve the payment mechanism via his contacts holding European cards.

notable.note: Two things a principal should see. First, the prospect disclosed a metabolic syndrome diagnosis and a kidney-stone history unprompted, the rep acknowledged it with 'Oh yeah, yeah, yeah' and never returned to it, then recommended time-restricted eating plus periodic extended fasts 'to completely flush through your body' — no clinician question was asked at any point. Second, the payment route on the table is a Russian resident sending roubles to friends holding European cards who then transfer $6,000 onward, with crypto raised by the rep as an alternative; nobody checked whether that is permissible. Separately, this call documents the actual payment-plan tiering — three payments at $6,000, six at $7,200 — which the same rep described the same day on another call as something 'we don't have anything set usually for'.
